$schema-note: Canonical Sondalab design tokens. Edit here only; run pnpm gen:tokens.

shared.$font-note: Type (ui-kit 0.30, Lumen): the UI is Geist and Geist Mono; display is Geist too, set 600 with negative tracking. Fraunces is the brand face only (--sl-font-brand: the wordmark and the monogram). The first family of every stack is vendored in packages/ui-kit/assets/fonts and declared in fonts.css (scripts/font-coverage.test.mjs). --sl-text-micro (10.5px) is the micro-label register: mono, uppercase, +0.06em.
shared.$radius-note: Lumen radii (ui-kit 0.31): md 8px (controls, fields, callouts), lg 14px (cards, dialogs, overlays), pane 10px (an island pane, between the two). sm stays 6px (rows, tiles, small chrome).
shared.$motion-ease-note: Two curves since ui-kit 0.31 (Lumen): --sl-motion-ease, cubic-bezier(0.25, 1, 0.5, 1), for every state change; --sl-motion-enter, cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1), a longer settle for what arrives (a dialog, a tooltip, a toast). Durations stay --sl-motion-fast|mid|slow, which reduced motion zeroes.
shared.$motion-spring-note: --sl-motion-spring: a damped spring (stiffness 170, damping 18) sampled into a CSS linear() easing — one ~5% overshoot, then settles. Time-normalised, so it plays at whatever duration token the transition uses. Only for transforms: on a colour the overshoot has no meaning. Re-scope R2 (card spring-tokens), 2026-09-25.
shared.$shadow-note: Casts (ui-kit 0.31, Lumen): black at the alpha each ground needs, never a tinted ink (the pre-0.31 cool ink rgba(28,29,34) is gone). sm is the short cast under a raised tile or key, md a small floating surface, lg the overlay cast (three layers: the overlay's own border in shade is its ring), inset the sunken well of a field. The :root value is the light ramp; each theme re-declares its own in the top-level shadow block.
shared.$viz-note: Categorical data-viz ramp (--sl-viz-0..7): distinct hues for arbitrary series / one-per-item colouring (agent walls, event kinds). Print-ink hues (vermilion, ultramarine, olive, ochre, …). The value here is the no-theme default (the dark ramp) emitted on :root; each theme re-declares the ramp at the lightness that clears 3:1 on its own grounds — see the top-level `viz` block. Not brand accents; independent of --sl-accent-*.

$neutrals-note: The neutral ladder (ui-kit 0.29, Lumen): one [oklch L, C] per role per theme. The generator tints it with each product's accent hue — the token accent for default, agent/accent-registry.json light/dark for every other product, following `inherits` — and bakes LITERAL HEX: themes/{light,dark}.css carry the default product's, themes/products.css every product's under [data-sl-product], neutrals.json all of them for hex-only consumers (Monaco, xterm, Electron, preload, sl-audit). Borders are the generated primary text at the alphas below, and so is the light overlay (`overlay`; dark's stays a black literal in themes.dark); border-lit is white. Chroma stays under 0.04 (colour.js isChromatic): the build fails above it, on gamut clipping, and on two products with different hues baking to identical neutrals. A registry edit is therefore a token change. Paper text-primary sits at L 0.23, not the Lumen mock's 0.2: the glass glint mirrors its lightness (1.2 - l) at the same chroma and must stay inside sRGB for any hue (the generator checks it). code-null is code-comment. High contrast keeps its literals in themes.high-contrast (tile = raised, sunken = canvas, lit = its white edge); any other --sl-* light or dark declares and high contrast does not own is reset to `initial` there, so a high-contrast island inherits nothing.
$code-note: Syntax-highlight palette (--sl-code-<role>): code is viz, out of the single-brand-accent scope — a chromatic code token stays semantically stable and readable, it does not track the product hue. Print inks, the same family as status and viz; every role clears 4.5:1 (comment/null 3:1) on canvas, surface, raised, tile and sunken of every product. The two neutral roles, fg and comment (null is comment), are rungs of the neutral ladder (`neutrals`), so they take the product's tint like every other neutral. Emitted per theme; high-contrast intentionally omitted (undefined there, consumers fall back).
$viz-theme-note: Per-theme --sl-viz-0..7, emitted into each theme file after shared.viz on :root. High-contrast reuses the dark ramp (its ground is black).
$spectrum-note: Prism (light theme only). --sl-spectrum-0..5 is light (glow: aurora bloom, press, haze), never text, never the only carrier of a meaning. --sl-spectrum-ink-0..4 is the same wheel darkened to >= 3:1 on the light grounds, for anything seen at 1px or as text (rims, aurora --rim/--linear, glitch, halftone, spectral text). Other themes reset both to `initial` so consumers fall back to their accent-derived colour. Not an accent: it never tracks the product hue and never marks state.
$shadow-theme-note: Per-theme --sl-shadow-* (0.31, Lumen): black on every theme, at about 2.6x the light alpha on the dark grounds, where a cast needs it to read. The values follow the Lumen reference's casts with its 1px ring left out: a surface that casts carries its own edge in shade. High-contrast reuses dark (components.css turns depth off there).
